title: Support Sculptor: ephemeral admin helper daemon to surface validated runbook actions in ticket context
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: First-line support often needs to execute short, well-scoped remediation steps that are documented in long-form runbooks. Switchover between ticket UI, runbook docs, and the admin console causes context loss and increases time-to-resolution. Goal: build a lightweight, ephemeral sidecar daemon (support-sculptor) that attaches to ticket/session context and surfaces a curated list of validated runbook actions (typed steps) that can be executed via a guarded API with audit logs and automatic rollback hooks. The daemon must be tiny (single process), language-agnostic for step adapters, respect RBAC and approval gates, and emit step-level telemetry for quality/regression monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar process can be launched per-support-session and register a session token with the control plane
Control plane returns a ranked list of up to 8 validated runbook steps based on ticket metadata (service, error-code, recent deploy)
Selected step can be executed via the sidecar with a single REST call and returns structured outcome (status, logs, artifacts)
Every execution emits telemetry: step_id, outcome, latency, actor, request_token, and a sanitized diff for sensitive outputs
RBAC enforced: only users with 'support:execute' can run 'danger' steps; approval flow exists for high-impact steps
Automatic rollback path is available for each step and can be invoked if outcome == failure or explicit rollback requested
E2E test harness validates happy path and failure path including rollback and audit log entry creation
implementation_notes: Phase 1: implement sidecar with small Go binary exposing local REST + unix-domain socket for ticket UI to call
Phase 2: control plane endpoint that returns validated steps based on a deterministic matcher (service, tags, recent alerts)
Step schema: id, short_title, description, input_schema (typed), command_adapter (shell|k8s|api), rollback_step_id, risk_level
Adapters implemented as sandboxed execors with timeouts and resource limits; default adapter is dry-run-enabled
Audit: every step execution writes to central audit log via secure gRPC; include cryptographic nonce for non-repudiation
Secrets: sidecar never stores credentials; uses ephemeral short-lived tokens minted by control plane and KMS-backed signing
testing_plan: Unit tests for matcher heuristics with 100+ synthetic ticket vectors
Integration tests: sidecar -> control plane -> audit service using local test harness
Chaos tests: simulate adapter failures, control-plane timeouts, and test rollback invariants
Security tests: role-scoped attempts to run denied steps, token expiration, and attempt replay
Load test: 200 concurrent support sessions to ensure sidecar + control plane scales with connection pooling
rollout_plan: Dogfood in internal support channel (support-team) for 2 weeks with verbose telemetry and kill-switch
Canary to 10% of sessions for one week using feature flag 'support-sculptor.canary'
Monitor step success rate, execution latency, and aborted rollbacks; target < 2% critical failures before ramp
Gradual rollout to 100% with 24/7 oncall coverage for first 48 hours
Post-mortem template auto-created on any failed rollback
